I farm beans on this small plot near my house, less than one hectare. I have no money to buy fertilizer from the shop, and beans grow fine without it like my mother taught me — they make the soil good by themselves. I keep my seeds from last harvest like always, and I put some goat droppings I gather from around the compound. My children and I will weed when the rains come, and if the pods get the small insects bad, my neighbor sometimes shares a little spray, but mostly I just pick them off.
